results.name: oil_symptom_routes_to_diagnostic_scan
results.description: Elimination-test ruling 2026-08-14 (Waleed): an oil change does NOT fix a burning-oil smell or consumption (valve-cover seep, stem seals), so the symptom coexists with a true record — the trust gate does NOT apply; the correct route is get_vehicle_health (mandatory read) then render_book_service with diagnostic-scan prefill. Also validates the 2026-08-14 classifier retune: a burning-OIL smell without smoke is severity soon (below the override) — turn 1 asserts no stop-driving language. turns.user: My engine smells like burning oil after I drive
turns.text:
Burning oil smell after driving is worth a closer look. A few things can cause it — worn valve-cover gaskets leaking onto hot surfaces, PCV issues, or internal wear pushing oil past the rings. Your oil change is on-time from two months ago, so it's not about fresh oil quantity.

One quick question: is the smell strongest right after you shut down, or do you notice it while driving? And any smoke or oil spots under the car?

turns.user: Mainly after long highway drives — no smoke anywhere, no leaks I can see
turns.text:
Burning oil smell after highway driving with no smoke or leaks visible — that's classic internal oil consumption, not a leak. The temperature warning light adds a wrinkle though. Here's what's likely: prolonged high-speed driving heats the engine harder, and worn valve seals or piston rings let oil past into the combustion chamber. That's internal wear, not something an oil change fixes.

The temperature warning is a separate concern — overheating compounds internal wear fast. You need a mechanic to confirm both are real (scan for codes, check coolant, eyeball the valve cover and oil cap for seeps). A Diagnostic Scan pins down whether this is just heavy consumption or if there's an active cooling issue making it worse.

Want to book that now?

turns.user: Oil level does seem to drop a bit between changes too
turns.text:
That confirms it's consumption, not just smell — oil dropping between changes plus the burning scent on highway drives points to internal burn-off or valve-seal seep. The temperature warning adds another layer worth checking in the same visit.

Booking a Diagnostic Scan now gets a BMW specialist to confirm whether it's normal consumption for the engine, accelerating valve seals, or the cooling system contributing. You'll have a real answer before any work.

turns.user: My oil light came on briefly then went off
turns.text:
Pull over as soon as it's safe and shut the engine off. Don't drive it any further — an oil-pressure warning means your engine's running without lubrication, and that can cause catastrophic damage within minutes.

Here's the thing: the fact that it went off doesn't mean it's fine. Oil-pressure warnings are serious because they give you almost no time before something breaks. Even a brief flicker is worth taking seriously.

If you want to check it yourself, there's one thing that sometimes clears this — the oil level might be low. I can walk you through exactly where to look and what to do if you want to try. If you'd rather not, or you're not sure, that's completely fine — we'll get you booked with a mechanic instead, and that's actually the safer call.

What's your call — want to check the oil yourself, or would you rather skip straight to getting a shop to look at it?
